title: continuously asks for .NET installed when is currently up to date
summary: Installed runtimes are already documented; the missing discriminator is the exact executable and framework requested by the prompt.

evidence: The report names a Microsoft Store installation of 0.102.2933 and repeated runtime prompts at Windows startup despite reinstalling. The exact dialog and failing executable are not supplied.
A diagnostic ZIP is already attached under Other Software, not the bug-report field; it was downloaded and inspected.
The supplied runtime inventory already lists .NETCore and WindowsDesktop runtimes through .NET 10, including 10.0.14; asking simply to install the latest .NET would ignore this evidence.
The attached Color Picker logs show successful earlier starts, but no current runtime-host prompt details. This does not identify which startup component now prompts.
Read the complete issue and attachment and inspected runtime inventory, install-file manifest, Color Picker log and its event-viewer entry; no comment or linked owner/fix is present.

Current ColorPickerUI.csproj imports Common.SelfContained.props and enables Windows App SDK self-contained deployment. This is current-source packaging evidence, not proof of the installed executable runtime configuration.
Related historical #20266 also reports installed runtimes and a prompt, but its old version does not establish a current duplicate or covering fix.
Bounded upstream/fork and runtime-title searches found no concrete implementation linked to this report. The exact host-requested framework/version/architecture is the next discriminator.
judgment.recommended_action: Request the expanded runtime dialog once, not another general bug report or an instruction to install the latest .NET.
judgment.rationale: Reinstallation did not help and the report lists modern desktop runtimes. No exact dialog or component identity establishes whether the failure is architecture, host resolution or deployment related.

fix_assessment.rationale: A component-specific correction is only a hypothesis pending the exact runtime-host request; no covering implementation or proven missing runtime has been identified.

proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: the prompting component resolves a different runtime/architecture or deployment payload from the installed runtimes listed in the report. The prompting executable is unknown, so a missing .NET major version or a Color Picker root cause is not established.
proposed_fixes.title: runtime-host resolution investigation
verification: Reproduce startup with the same Store installation and architecture.
Verify the identified component launches without a runtime prompt with the supported deployment payload.
Test that other modules and the supported architecture variants retain their intended runtime behavior.

confidence.rationale: The source identifies a plausible boundary, but this pass did not reproduce the failing transition. The accompanying diagnostic action distinguishes competing explanations.

plan: Identify the prompting executable and requested framework/version/architecture from the dialog.
Compare that component runtime configuration and effective host resolution with the supplied installed-runtime inventory and expected release payload.
Only if a packaging or launch-path mismatch is confirmed, design a correction at that boundary rather than prescribe another broad reinstall.

comment.body: Thanks for the attached report and for checking reinstalling. I inspected the ZIP linked under Other Software: it already lists .NET and Windows Desktop runtimes through .NET 10, so another general report or simply installing the latest .NET is not the next step. Please upload the full runtime prompt through the GitHub web UI, expanding More information if available, or paste its app/executable name, requested framework/version and architecture with personal paths removed. Does it appear immediately at login or only when invoking a particular module? This distinguishes a different host/runtime target from a deployment problem.
